articles.title: “It’s a full commitment from the full family”: How Patrick Mahomes’ ACL rehab tested Brittany Mahomes strength at home with their 3 kids
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes spent much of his 2026 offseason working through a serious knee injury.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes spent much of his 2026 offseason working through a serious knee injury. While the Chiefs quarterback focused on his recovery, Brittany Mahomes took on more at home with their three children. Mahomes recently opened up about that side of his comeback, giving Brittany credit for keeping their family routine going while he spent long hours at the rehab facility.The comment came as Mahomes prepared for Kansas City’s Week 4 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders. Speaking with Mitch Holthus on “The Chiefs Kingdom Show” at Arrowhead Stadium earlier this week, Mahomes explained that his recovery affected the whole family. He also revealed why getting back to his children became one of his biggest personal goals. How Brittany Mahomes took over more at home while Patrick Mahomes focused on his recoveryMahomes did not go through his rehab alone, but his wife carried a different part of the load.In a recent interview, Mahomes explained that Brittany had to take on more responsibility because he spent much of the offseason away from home. The quarterback said he spent about seven hours a day at the rehab facility when the family would normally spend that time together on vacation or back in Texas.“She had to kind of take on that role on even more because I wasn’t at the house,” Mahomes said during “The Chiefs Kingdom Show.”That meant Brittany handled more of the daily routine with their three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden. Sterling is 5, Bronze is 3, and Golden is 20 months old, according to the Heavy report.Mahomes then gave his wife direct credit for keeping the household together.“It’s a full commitment from the full family,” he said during the same Arrowhead interview. He added that Brittany did “a great job” leading the household while he worked at the rehab facility.Brittany later shared a clip of Mahomes’ comments on her Instagram Stories and responded, “Would do anything for my babies and my husband.”That response added another layer to Mahomes’ comments. His return to football required daily work from him, but family life still needed attention while he spent those hours rehabbing. Why getting back to his kids became a major part of Patrick Mahomes’ comebackThe family angle goes beyond Brittany handling more at home. Mahomes has also explained how his injury changed his role as a father.During Chiefs training camp on July 24, 2026, Steve Walls asked Mahomes about the toughest mental hurdle during his rehab. Mahomes did not point to missing football. Instead, he talked about his children.“Honestly, the toughest part was at the beginning, not being able to get up and chase my kids around,” Mahomes said at training camp.He explained that being active with his children has always been important to him. Once his recovery allowed him to move around with them again, that progress gave him another reason to keep pushing.Mahomes specifically mentioned Bronze’s T-ball games and Sterling’s soccer activities. Being able to attend those moments gave him a clear sign that his recovery was moving forward.Mahomes suffered the knee injury during Kansas City’s Week 15 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers in December 2025. He later spent roughly nine months working toward his return, with his children becoming part of the motivation behind that process.Now, as the Chiefs move through the 2026 season, Mahomes’ comeback carries a personal story beyond the football field. His rehab demanded long hours from him, while Brittany helped keep their family life moving. articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. expected to play for Cowboys in Week 4 after missing start of season with back injury
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr. is feeling better after a mid-week trade to the Cowboys.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is healed. After missing the start of the season due to a back injury, Porter is expected to play in Week 4 after being traded to the Cowboys, according to ESPN.

Porter, however, is expected to have his snaps limited during the contest.

It will mark the first game all season in which Porter has played. The 26-year-old missed the first three weeks of the regular season due to both back and conditioning issues. Despite being able to put in work during practices, Porter was constantly ruled out on game days by the Pittsburgh Steelers after missing time in the offseason due to a contract dispute.

That dispute ultimately resulted in the Steelers trading Porter to the Cowboys on Wednesday. The Cowboys sent a sixth-round pick and a second-round pick to the Steelers as part of the deal.

Following the trade, Porter was not listed among the Cowboys' injuries and received no injury designation on the team's final report, suggesting he would suit up in Week 4 against the Houston Texans.

While there's an uncharitable read on the situation that suggests Porter was never truly hurt and was sitting out over his contract situation in Pittsburgh, the limited snap count for Porter in Week 4 does suggest there are legitimate concerns about immediately throwing him into a game.

Porter, who is in the final year of his rookie contract, was at odds with the Steelers all offseason over a contract extension. There was a hard deadline on a deal getting done, as the Steelers — generally — do not negotiate contracts during the season. That deadline passed without a deal, putting Porter and the team at an impasse.

That impasse was solved with Wednesday's trade. Though he still doesn't have a contract extension, Porter will reportedly take the field for the Cowboys in Week 4. If he can go out and turn in a strong season, Porter should eventually get the mega-contract he's seeking, whether from the Cowboys or from another franchise once he hits the free-agent market.

articles.title: Tony Pollard among NFL trade deadline targets to watch, per report
articles.summary: ESPN reported that Titans running back Tony Pollard is a player to watch in the weeks leading into the NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline is still more than a month away, but chatter is already starting after a couple trades this week.

ESPN's Adam Schefter, reporting on the network's "Sunday NFL Countdown" pregame show on Oct. 4, mentioned Titans running back Tony Pollard as a player to watch among NFL trade targets before the Nov. 10 deadline.

Pollard, 29, has rushed for at least 1,000 yards in each of the last four seasons, including the last two with Tennessee.

The Memphis alum "fits the profile" as a trade target, Schefter reported, given the Titans' slow start and his contract.

Pollard is in the final year of a three-year deal signed in 2024 as the Titans aimed to replace Derrick Henry. He has a base salary of $6.74 million this year with $510,000 in roster bonuses spread across the season, per Spotrac.

The veteran back has been the Titans' clear No. 1 back through three weeks in terms of touches and production despite Tyjae Spears playing 44% of offensive snaps.

Tennessee also has rookie running back Nicholas Singleton and veterans Julius Chestnut and Michael Carter on the roster.

articles.title: Marcus Mariota ruled out in Week 4 with right knee injury, Commanders already down Jayden Daniels
articles.summary: The Commanders are already without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels in Week 4.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders came into Week 4 dealing with multiple significant injuries on offense. Early in the contest, they were dealt another one, as quarterback Marcus Mariota was forced to leave the game after a first-quarter sack.

The play occurred on Washington's second drive of the game. With the team deep in Indianapolis Colts' territory, Mariota was sacked on a third-and-goal. The Commanders were forced to kick a field goal at the end of the drive, taking a 6-0 lead.

Mariota headed to the blue tent on the sideline before being taken back to the locker room. The Commanders eventually announced a right knee injury for Mariota. He was initially deemed questionable to return before being ruled out before the start of the third quarter.

On the team's next drive, Athan Kaliakmanis entered the game as the team's starting quarterback. The drive marked Kaliakmanis' NFL debut. The team selected him out of Rutgers in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft.

Mariota's injury comes at an awful time for the Commanders. The team came into Sunday's contest without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels, backup running back Rashaad White and No. 1 receiver Terry McLaurin.

While the Commanders' offense stalled twice with Mariota under center — settling for field goals — the veteran had shown some big-play potential before going down. Prior to leaving the game, Mariota had a 35-yard rush and found running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on a short gain that wound up going for 35 yards.

Kaliakmanis could not get anything going offensively for the Commanders, leading to the team falling behind 10-6 at halftime.
